posts.author: Kabir_B
posts.text: Rs 1 Lakh to Rs 9,200: The Kore Digital Story — The subsidiary part is really interesting… ₹21cr to ₹408cr revenue in just a few years, with around 75% coming from subsidiaries. And some of those were acquired just months after being incorporated. Makes you wonder if this was a way to inflate the books and show a much bigger growth story than what was actually happening… Also makes you realise how little we sometimes look beyond the headline numbers before getting carried away by the growth story.

posts.author: Norton_Fernandes
posts.text: Rs 1 Lakh to Rs 9,200: The Kore Digital Story — SME stocks can be really dangerous. ₹1 lakh to ₹9,200 is a painful reminder of that. When the price keeps going up, it’s easy to stop questioning the story. At some point the chart starts looking better than the actual business Worth checking the numbers, cash flows and related-party transactions before getting too carried away. Fundamental investing always stays evergreen.

posts.author: Rohith_Raj
posts.text: Rs 1 Lakh to Rs 9,200: The Kore Digital Story — Kore Digital has come under SEBI’s scanner after the regulator raised questions about the company’s reported financials. SEBI says Kore acquired several subsidiaries and then consolidated their revenues into its own financials. The regulator has alleged that some of these subsidiaries were not genuine businesses. Around ₹541 crore of revenue reported in FY25 and FY26 may have been misstated, mainly through certain subsidiaries that the regulator says may not have been genuine businesses.
